app_store.name: Controller-9
app_store.subtitle: Your phone is the controller
app_store.promotional_text: New: move and resize any button, and a connection check that tells you why the computer can't be reached. Free, no ads, no account.
app_store.description:
Controller-9 turns your iPhone into a game controller for your computer.

Pair once with the free Controller-9 companion on your computer (Windows, Mac or Linux). On Windows and Linux, games see an Xbox 360 controller; on a Mac the companion plays games as keyboard and mouse.

What you get:
- Seven familiar layouts, plus your own: move and resize any button
- Tilt steering measured from however you hold the phone
- Rumble from the game, felt on the phone
- Every press tested: an automated test presses each control and checks it arrives as itself
- A connection check that says why the computer can't be reached, and the fix

Free. No ads, no subscription, no account, no analytics. Local network only.
app_store.whats_new: Move and resize any button on any layout. A connection check names the cause and the fix. GameCube and arcade stick layouts.

google_play.title: Controller-9
google_play.short_description: Your phone pairs as an Xbox controller over Bluetooth. Nothing to install.
google_play.full_description:
Controller-9 turns your Android phone into a game controller.

Nothing to install on the computer: turn on Bluetooth controller, then choose "Xbox Wireless Controller" in the computer's Bluetooth settings. Games see a standard Xbox controller.

What you get:
- Seven familiar layouts: Xbox, DualSense, DualShock 4, Switch Pro, 8BitDo Pro 2 and GameCube styles, plus an arcade stick
- Move and resize any button on its own
- Tilt steering measured from however you hold the phone, and gyro aim
- Rumble from the game, felt on the phone
- Turbo and toggle buttons, a layout and colour per game
- A connection check that says why the computer can't be reached, and the fix
- Controller Lock: no notification panel or back swipes mid-game

Tested on a Mac with a game (Xbox button prompts), in Safari and Chrome as a standard gamepad, and on Linux through SDL. Windows and Linux can also use the free companion app.

Free. No ads, no subscription, no account, no analytics. Local network and Bluetooth only.
